svg.text: Why sun4u needs a trap table before it can have an MMU
UltraSPARC has no hardware page-table walker. Every TLB miss is a software trap — so the MMU and the trap table are one problem, not two.
Load, store, or instruction fetch issues a virtual address + context id
I-TLB / D-TLB lookup — 64 fully-associative entries each, 8 KB base page size
Hardware only. This is the entire extent of the hardware's involvement in translation.
HIT — the common case
Physical address produced, execution continues. No software involved.
MISS — a trap, every single time
There is no walker. Software must resolve this or the CPU stops.
Hardware does exactly three favours, then gets out of the way
1 · latches faulting VA + context into TLB Tag Access
2 · precomputes a TSB pointer from TSB Base and the hashed VA
3 · vectors to a fixed offset in the trap table at %tba
Our asm fast path — a handful of instructions, no stack, no C
Load the candidate TTE from the TSB, compare its tag against the
faulting VA. It runs on every miss, so its cost is the port's
steady-state memory performance.
Tag matches
stxa the TTE straight
into the TLB, then
retry the instruction.
Tag misses
Fall out to C: walk the
Haiku translation map,
refill TSB, or fault.
What this means for the work plan
The TSB is ours to own
A direct-mapped, software-managed cache of TTEs
in ordinary physical memory. Haiku must allocate
it, point the TSB register at it, and keep it
coherent with VMTranslationMap on every unmap.
The handler lives in the trap table
It cannot be a normal function — it runs with no
usable stack. So Phase "MMU" and Phase "traps"
cannot be sequenced; they ship together.
Two TLBs, two contexts, two demap paths
I and D MMUs are separate, each with its own ASI
block. Primary vs. secondary context is the
mechanism that lets a kernel in its own address
space still reach user memory — see ticket #19597.
Register and ASI layout: UltraSPARC-IIi User's Manual — MMU overview p.23, demap operations pp.85–86, TLB/TSB register block Table 6-10.
Those constants are already transcribed in Haiku's src/system/kernel/arch/sparc/arch_mmu.cpp — the reading side exists; the managing side does not.
